description: We are students at the School of Technical Sciences at Kırklareli University. As five people who love computer science, we’ve come here to give it our all in this competition. I wish all my fellow competitors the best of luck.
summary: AEGIS-BIO is an offline-first astronaut health monitoring and mission control software suite written in Rust (eframe/egui, rusqlite, tokio) for deep-space and orbital exploration. Addressing the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge, it pairs an autonomous wrist and tablet Astronaut Biomonitor (biomon-mobile for Android and desktop) with a habitat Flight Surgeon Hub (hub-desktop). Mapped directly to NASA's Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight, the engine evaluates 1 Hz biometrics, cabin and EVA suit atmospheres, space radiation flux, 60-second actigraphy sleep epochs, nutrition, SANS, osteoporosis protection, and Haldane decompression ratios across LAUNCH, ORBIT, EVA, and REENTRY corridors. Grounded in NASA OSDR studies (OSD-569, OSD-575, OSD-656), RadLab, EDA (RR-1), and JPL Horizons Earth-Mars light-delay data, AEGIS-BIO buffers all telemetry locally in SQLite WAL during communication blackouts and delivers glove-friendly color-coded alerts (GREEN/ORANGE/RED) plus clear offline countermeasures when Earth support is unreachable.
details:
Overview & Mission Need

Long-duration Artemis and Mars missions expose astronauts to extended habitat link blackouts and one-way Earth light delays exceeding 10 minutes (10.5–11.0 min in November 2026 derived from NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data). Crews cannot depend on ground or cloud servers during acute anomalies such as cabin CO2 buildup, EVA suit depressurization, solar particle radiation spikes, hypoxia, or orthostatic intolerance. AEGIS-BIO equips both the individual astronaut and the habitat Flight Surgeon with immediate, self-explanatory, offline-first health monitoring and actionable countermeasures.

What It Does & How It Works

AEGIS-BIO runs as a two-node pure-Rust Cargo workspace communicating over zero-configuration local networking (UDP discovery beacon, .1 gateway probe, and subnet sweep to TCP NDJSON port 7878) with optional Windows Wi-Fi Direct / Mobile Hotspot SoftAP hosting (AEGIS-HUB):

  • Astronaut Biomonitor (biomon-mobile): Cross-platform tactile HUD targeting ARM64 Android wearables/tablets (aarch64-linux-android, minSdk 26) and desktop simulation (biomon-desktop-runner). Its 4-quadrant cockpit (HEALTH & SUIT, HUB & NAV, COMMS, HAZARD & ENV) switches cleanly between VIEW Mode (#4CB944 green border on a high-glare #F0F0E4 daylight surface) and INPUT Mode (#FF8929 orange border, ≥26 pt glove-friendly touch targets for logging ISS meals at 25%/50%/100% consumption, hydration, exercise, simulation scenarios, RF blackout testing, and local alert acknowledgements), with #CD0929 crimson danger overrides.
  • Mission Control Hub (hub-desktop): Multi-crew Flight Surgeon workstation auto-provisioning up to 6 crew slots (AST-01 to AST-06) across four synchronized tabs: Crew Vitals Monitor, Phase & Stress Control (LAUNCH, ORBIT, EVA, REENTRY phases plus 6 fault injection scenarios), Medical & Incident Log (clinical notes plus NASA OSDR lab panel comparisons), and Food Catalog & Sync (daily nutrition, SANS/osteoporosis scoring, and SHA-256 dataset provenance verification).
  • Offline-First SQLite WAL Synchronization: Both local nodes persist state in SQLite Write-Ahead Logging databases (aegis_biomon.db and aegis_hub.db). During communication blackouts, 1 Hz telemetry frames, manual crew inputs, and 60-second actigraphy sleep epochs queue locally and reconcile automatically without duplicates on reconnect via composite keys (astronaut_id + edge_seq_id / edge_input_id).

Addressing NASA's Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight

  • Space Radiation: Continuous uSv/hr dose monitoring benchmarked against NASA OSDR RadLab (Liulin-5-D3) absorbed dose series (>50 uSv/hr triggers hazard alerts and RADIATION shielding countermeasures).
  • Isolation & Confinement: 60-second actigraphy sleep epoch classification (SLEEP/WAKE efficiency against a 480-minute sleep target) and crew behavioral/isolation self-report check-ins (ISOLATION_SURVEY).
  • Distance from Earth: Full autonomous bedside warning and countermeasure execution offline, paired with dynamic Earth-Mars one-way light delay calculation (distance_au × 8.31675 min/AU) from JPL Horizons ephemeris data.
  • Gravity Fields: Continuous Shock Index (HR/SBP > 0.90 alert), G-load orthostatic risk classification (HIGH at >2.5 G with low SBP), 1-compartment Haldane nitrogen washout (360-minute half-time, blood_n2_idx > 1.50 alert), and daily Osteoporosis Protection scoring from exercise load, calcium (mg), and vitamin D3 (IU).
  • Hostile Closed Environments: Real-time cabin CO2 (>3000 ppm danger), cabin O2 (<19.5% danger), EVA suit pressure (<25.0 kPa breach danger), and cumulative dietary sodium plus cabin CO2 SANS risk scoring (HIGH ≥ 70), contextualized with NASA OSDR EDA (RR-1) ISS vs. ground baselines and OSDR OSD-569/575/656 immune/metabolic/cardiovascular biomarker studies.

Benefits, Impact & Technical Innovation

By pairing plain-language deterministic protocols (CARDIO, DECOMP, HYDRATION, HYPOXIA, RADIATION) tailored for non-physician crew self-care with multi-crew clinical oversight for flight surgeons, AEGIS-BIO reduces diagnostic latency in deep space and adapts directly to terrestrial analog habitats, submarines, saturation diving, and remote disaster medicine. Engineering safeguards include Rust memory safety, NaN/non-finite telemetry fail-safe alerts in calc.rs, idempotent SQLite schemas, and SHA-256 dataset provenance tracking in sqlite (dataset_provenance).

Tools, Languages, Frameworks & Platforms

  • Languages: Rust (2024 edition), Python 3.11+ (NASA dataset ETL pipeline scripts/build_nasa_seed.py)
  • Core Libraries: eframe / egui 0.37 (GPU immediate-mode HUD), rusqlite 0.32 (bundled SQLite WAL), tokio 1 (async TCP/UDP LAN sync), serde / serde_json (NDJSON wire protocol), windows 0.62.2 (WinRT WiFiDirect / NetworkOperators SoftAP hosting)
  • Targets: Windows x64 executable (hub-desktop.exe) and Android ARM64 APK (aegis-biomon.apk, minSdk 26)

Team Los Galacticos (5 Members — Kırklareli University School of Technical Sciences)

  • Emir Samed Yalçınkaya — Project Lead, Physiological & Risk Engine, SQLite Schema & LAN Sync
  • Emre Düzcan — Systems Architecture, Workspace Modularization & Cross-Platform Application Scaffold
  • Ege Canbaz — UI Architecture & Extended Tactile Interface Engineering
  • Emin Sancaklı — Dataset Research & NASA Open Data Integration Analysis
  • Harun Karakoyun — Research & General Project Support

Transparency & Use of Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure

In accordance with NASA Space Apps rules: LLM-assisted coding and documentation tools supported rapid Rust/SQLite prototyping, ETL script scaffolding, test assistance, English technical editing, and slide layout structuring. All physiological equations, safety corridors, NASA dataset normalization rules, test validations (cargo test --workspace), and architectural designs were verified and integrated by Team Los Galacticos. All embedded interface screenshots are direct captures of our Rust HUD application and contain zero NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers.
